prompt: Build VersionTag: parse "1.2.10" or "2.0.0-beta", then make compareTo, equals, hashCode and toString all agree so TreeSet and HashSet see the same duplicates. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: compareTo returning 0 and equals returning true are supposed to mean the same thing, and this exercise makes the reason concrete: a TreeSet judges duplicates with compareTo while a HashSet uses hashCode and equals, so the two collections only agree when the three methods agree. Defining equals as compareTo(other) == 0 guarantees that by construction, and hashCode must then be built from exactly the four values compareTo looks at. Comparing the numbers as ints rather than as text is what makes 1.10.0 sort after 1.9.9.
hints: Split the optional suffix off at the first '-' before splitting the rest on "\\.", and validate that you got exactly three all-digit parts.
In compareTo use Integer.compare for each of the three numbers and return as soon as one of them differs.
For the tie-break, treat an empty pre-release as the highest: a tag with a suffix sorts before the same tag without one, and two suffixes compare with String.compareTo.
